inspiration: repipe round 4 need pe-header-entry-mapped; the shape is the PE half of what the ELF path already gets for free -- an ELF's PT_LOAD headers describe the header bytes that are in the mapping, a PE's section table does not
decisions: The refuter's hypothesis is UPHELD and its mechanism was exact. loadimage_object.rs builds its map from file.segments(), which for a PE is the section list; nothing anywhere published the SizeOfHeaders bytes Windows maps at ImageBase, so vma_is_mapped() answered false at 0x400154 and the entry could not be selected by any route.

Read-only DATA, not CODE, as the refuter's two controls already showed sufficient. Beyond matching PAGE_READONLY it is what makes the change safe to default on: entry discovery scans executable regions, so a non-executable header page cannot add a phantom entry to the 17 in-repo and 163 dataset PEs. Measured, not argued -- `kuna functions --json` is byte-identical across 57 PE images.

The region rides a new ObjectFormat::header_region with a None default rather than a format branch in the load path, so ELF/Mach-O/COFF are unreachable by construction and the boundary keeps its stated role as the single funnel for per-format knowledge.

Clamped to min(SizeOfHeaders, file length, first section RVA). The first-section clamp is the load-bearing one: SizeOfHeaders is a header field a packer is free to lie about, and without the clamp an inflated value would shadow section 1 -- which is exactly how the refuter's own control accidentally dropped that image from 2 functions to 0. A clamp to zero publishes no region rather than an empty one (unit-tested with a section at RVA 0).

No phases.toml option: a loader mapping unit cannot be a judgement call, the change is measured byte-identical on every image that loads today, and the tooling track's rule is that a strict correctness fix ships without a flag. Same disposition as the two sibling loader fixes this round (#451, #453).

promoted_probe.retargeted_from: dataset bin/BUG.cRYPTO.kEYGENME.zip.__x/BUG.exe (aPLib-packed PE32, AddressOfEntryPoint 0x154 inside a 0x200-byte header page)
promoted_probe.retargeted_to: decompiler/crates/kuna-analysis/tests/fixtures/pe_headerentry_i386.exe (1024-byte PE32 twin: e_lfanew 0x0c, 0xe0-byte optional header, two sections, section table 0x104..0x154, entry 0x154)
promoted_probe.why: CI has no dataset; the twin carries the identical defect at the identical address and exits 1 with the identical 'address 0x400154 is not mapped in this input' on the unpatched build
promoted_probe.verified_on_witness: the acceptance passed on the dataset original first: `kuna decompile BUG.exe 0x400154 --addr --define-function 0x400154=entry` goes from exit 1 to exit 0 emitting C for entry(), and `disassemble --addr 0x400154 --as code` decodes the aPLib-style bit-reader stub the refuter predicted

sweep.method: A/B by binary: the patched release kuna against one built from the recorded base commit with the four source files reverted, both replayed over every PE image in reach
sweep.pe_images_detail: all 17 in-repo MZ fixtures plus the 40 smallest of the 169 dataset PE images
sweep.xrefs_detail: `xrefs --to 0x400154` on the 3 images whose header page actually covers that address: target.name goes from null to sub_400154 because the address is now mapped. count stays 0 and the reference list is unchanged on all 57 -- i.e. the only movement is the fix itself, at an address deliberately chosen to be inside the header page.
sweep.why_not: the region is published read-only DATA below the first section's RVA, so it adds no CODE span (function extents and discovery both key on CODE) and overlaps nothing that was already mapped; the only new answers are at addresses that previously had none

speed_method: A/B by binary, interleaved ABBA over 11 rounds, warmup discarded; a sibling builder shared the box, so the run-to-run stdev (262 ms, ~6%) dwarfs the effect
speed_note: median -0.82%, min-of-11 +0.05%, i.e. indistinguishable from noise. Per PE load the added work is one typed header parse and a memcpy of at most SizeOfHeaders (0x200-0x400 bytes); a non-PE returns None before reading anything.
